span.term: Elevated baseline cortical noise degrades the mPFC's ability to form category-specific social representations and to drive the synaptic plasticity that refines them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Loss of CNTNAP2 impairs targeting of AMPA and NMDA receptors to post-synaptic membranes, removing the plasticity that would otherwise refine odour-category representations with experience
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The social/nonsocial distinction is a distinction between two sets of odours.
span.note: what this limits: any claim that this mPFC activity encodes social information: the tuning measure is the normalised odor-evoked response magnitude, and it was higher for male and female cues than for all nonsocial odors
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Two of the three behavioural measures did not differ between social and nonsocial stimuli.
span.note: what this limits: any behavioural evidence that the mice treated social cues differently: orientation probability was higher for social cues, while response latency and the stimulus-evoked increase in locomotion did not significantly differ

span.label: The paper's central quantity is a log ratio of distances between activity patterns.
span.note: what this limits: any social distinction index quoted from this work: it was calculated to quantify the separation between the representations of social and nonsocial stimuli for each mouse

span.label: In the mouse medial prefrontal cortex, nearly a quarter of recorded units were selective for social odours, twice as many as were selective for nonsocial odours or showed mixed responses.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The mPFC population code is organised by social versus nonsocial category rather than by odour identity or valence: responses to the two social cues were more similar to each other than to any nonsocial odour.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Average unit tuning was stronger for both male and female social cues than for any of the three nonsocial odours, independent of odour identity.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: In wild-type mice the social distinction index rose significantly from the first to the second recording day, showing experience-dependent refinement of the social representation.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Cntnap2 knockout mice showed no experience-dependent change: their social distinction index was unchanged between the two recording sessions.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The autism-model deficit is specific to categorisation rather than to stimulus encoding: single-odour decoding was equally accurate in both genotypes, but social/nonsocial category decoding was significantly worse in Cntnap2 knockouts.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Baseline (ongoing) population activity was noisier in Cntnap2 knockout mice than in wild-type littermates, with the two genotypes almost completely non-overlapping on this measure.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Mean baseline firing rates of mPFC units were higher in Cntnap2 knockout mice than in wild-type littermates.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Across both genotypes, the level of baseline neuronal noise was strongly negatively correlated with the social distinction index.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Baseline cortical noise predicted how much a mouse's social representation refined with experience: higher noise went with a smaller day-to-day gain in the social distinction index.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The neural preference for social cues was not explained by behaviour: latency to orient and stimulus-evoked locomotion did not differ between social and nonsocial odours.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
